record.summary: Overview of nine emerging safety processes and associated practices for frontier AI organisations, published by the UK government ahead of the AI Safety Summit of 1-2 November 2023 to inform companies' safety policies and help readers compare them. The processes are responsible capability scaling, model evaluations and red teaming, model reporting and information sharing, security controls including securing model weights, vulnerability reporting, identifiers of AI-generated material, prioritising research on AI risks, preventing and monitoring misuse, and data input controls and audits.
record.notes: Published with a companion page collecting frontier AI companies' safety policies, which the UK had encouraged companies to publish before the summit. The document describes itself as a snapshot that is not government policy that must be enacted and will need regular updating; six of its processes correspond to commitments many leading companies made in July 2023. GOV.UK shows it as published under the 2022 to 2024 Sunak Conservative government.

verification.note: Stored and read in this run: the GOV.UK publication page (last checked 17 Oct 2026, unchanged since 11 Oct) and the 45-page PDF. They confirm the title, DSIT as issuer, publication on 27 October 2023, the nine processes and the document's non-binding character; the page carries no withdrawal notice. Version 1's notes that it has not been formally replaced and was the forerunner of the Frontier AI Safety Commitments (INT-06) are not in these sources and were removed; the link to INT-06 stays in related.

summary.quote: This document sets out nine emerging processes and associated practices for frontier AI organisations' AI safety policies:
The UK has therefore encouraged frontier AI organisations to publish details on their frontier AI safety policies ahead of the AI Safety Summit hosted by the UK on 1-2 November 2023.
merely detailing the current suite available so that others can understand, interpret and compare frontier companies' safety policies
Responsible Capability Scaling provides a framework for managing risk as organisations scale capability of frontier AI systems.
Security Controls Including Securing Model Weights are key underpinnings for the safety of an AI system.
Identifiers of AI-generated Material provide additional information about whether content has been AI generated or modified.
Prioritising Research on Risks Posed by AI will help identify and address the emerging risks posed by frontier AI.
Preventing and Monitoring Model Misuse is important as, once deployed, AI systems can be intentionally misused for harmful outcomes.
Data Input Controls and Audits can help identify and remove training data likely to increase the dangerous capabilities
